accepted.question_text: Let r and p be integers with p ≥ 2. For symmetric deterministic tensors T1, …, Tn ∈ (R^d)^{⊗ r} and independent standard Gaussian variables g1, …, gn, define the symmetric injective ℓ_p norm by ||T||_{I_p} = max_{||x||_p ≤ 1} |⟨T, x^{⊗ r}⟩|. Is it true that there is a bound of the form E ||∑_{i=1}^n g_i T_i||_{I_p} ≤ Õ_{r,p}( d^{1/2 - 1/p} (∑_{i=1}^n ||T_i||_{I_p}^2)^{1/2} ), where Õ_{r,p} hides constants depending on r and p and polylogarithmic factors in d and n?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 16 (Type-2 constant of Tensors). Let p ≥ 2, then E ||∑_{i=1}^n g_i T_i||_{I_p} ≤ O˜_{r,p}( d^{1/2 - 1/p} √(∑_{i=1}^n ||T_i||_{I_p}^2) ).

accepted.question_text: If G is an Erdős–Rényi random graph distributed as G(n, 1/2), is its Lovász number asymptotically equal to √n in expectation, namely E[ϑ(G)] = (1 + o(1))√n as n → ∞?

evidence.quote: However, the precise asymptotics of the Lov´asz number for G(n, 1/2) is still open. Conjecture 17. Let G be distributed as G(n, 1/2). Then, Eϑ(G) = (1 + o(1))√n.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a random dense circulant graph on n vertices, sampled by choosing the neighbors of one vertex uniformly subject to circulant symmetry. Is its Lovász number also asymptotically √n in expectation, that is, does E[ϑ(G)] = (1 + o(1))√n hold as n → ∞?
accepted.context_brief: Lovász number of random circulant graphs

evidence.quote: We conjecture, based on numerical observations, that the Lov´asz number for random dense circulant graphs behaves similarly to that for G(n, 1/2). This motivates the following question. Conjecture 18. Let G be distributed as a random dense circulant graph. Then, Eϑ(G) = (1 + o(1))√n.

accepted.question_text: Fix M and let N = 4M − 5. Draw a complex matrix A ∈ C^{N×M} at random so that im(A) is uniformly distributed over the Grassmannian of M-dimensional subspaces of C^{4M−5} (for example, A may have i.i.d. Gaussian entries). If p_M denotes the probability that the phaseless measurement map x mod 𝕋 ↦ |Ax|^2 is injective, must one have (a) p_M < 1 for every M and (b) p_M → 0 as M → ∞?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 19. Let N = 4M − 5 and draw A ∈ C^{N×M} at random ... Let p_M be the probability that the mapping x mod T ↦ |Ax|^2 is injective. (a) p_M < 1 for all M. (b) lim_{M→∞} p_M = 0.

accepted.question_text: For a real matrix A ∈ R^{(2M−1)×M}, define ω(A) = min_{S ⊆ [N] : rank(A_{S^c}) < M} σ_M(A_S), where A_S is the submatrix formed by the rows indexed by S and σ_M denotes the smallest singular value. Suppose every subset of M rows of A spans R^M. Do there exist universal constants C > 0 and 0 < β < 1 such that ω(A) ≤ C max_{k ∈ [N]} ||A_k||^β for every such A, where A_k is the k-th row?
accepted.context_brief: Stability parameter for real phase retrieval

evidence.quote: Conjecture 20. There exist universal constants C > 0 and 0 < β < 1 such that, for any M > 1 and A ∈ R^{2M−1×M} a matrix for which any subset of M rows spans R^M, ω(A) ≤ C max_{k∈[N]} ||A_k||^β_M.

accepted.question_text: If A is a real matrix with i.i.d. standard Gaussian entries in the phase-retrieval setting above, what is the typical value of the stability quantity ω(A) = min_{S ⊆ [N] : rank(A_{S^c}) < M} σ_M(A_S)? In particular, does ω(A) satisfy a bound of the type conjectured above, and if so, what exponent β is valid?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 21. What is the value of ω(A) for A with iid standard gaussian entries? Does it satisfy the bound in the conjecture? If so, what is β?

accepted.question_text: Let MUB(d) denote the maximum number of pairwise mutually unbiased orthonormal bases in C^d. Is it true that in dimension 6 one cannot have a complete set of seven such bases, i.e. does MUB(6) < 7 hold?

evidence.quote: For d not a prime power, the problem of determining MUB(d) is still open. The smallest open instance is particularly well known for being a tantalizing open problem ... Conjecture 22. Let MUB(d) denote the largest possible number of (simultaneously) mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) in C^d. We have MUB(6) < 7.

accepted.question_text: Can one prove nonexistence of seven mutually unbiased bases in C^6 using a degree-4 Sum-of-Squares certificate? Equivalently, is there a degree-4 SoS proof that no collection of 7 × 6 vectors in C^6 can satisfy the mutually unbiased basis constraints for seven bases?

evidence.quote: It is however unclear whether higher degree levels of Sum-of-Squares can provide such a proof. Open Problem 23. Is there a Sum-of-Squares degree 4 proof that there are no 7 Mutually Unbiased Bases in C^6?

accepted.question_text: For every dimension d, does there exist an equiangular tight frame in C^d with exactly d^2 vectors, equivalently a symmetric informationally complete positive operator-valued measure (SIC-POVM) in every complex dimension?

evidence.quote: It is a well known conjecture that they exist for all dimensions d, known as Zauner’s Conjecture [Zau99]. Conjecture 24 (Zauner’s Conjecture). For each dimension d, there exists an ETF in C^d with n = d^2 vectors.

accepted.question_text: Let G_p be the Paley graph on a prime number p ≡ 1 (mod 4), and let ω(G_p) be its clique number. Is ω(G_p) bounded by a polylogarithmic function of p, i.e. does ω(G_p) = O(polylog(p)) hold?

evidence.quote: A random graph of the same degree has logarithmic clique number, which motivates the following well known conjecture ... Conjecture 25. Let ω(G_p) denote the clique number of the Paley Graph for p ≡ 1 (mod 4) prime. ω(G_p) = O(polylog(p)).

accepted.question_text: Let G_{p,1} be the induced subgraph of the Paley graph G_p on the vertices adjacent to 0 (the 1-localization). Is the Lovász theta number of this localized graph asymptotic to √(p/2), that is, does ϑ(G_{p,1}) ∼ √(p/2) as p → ∞ through primes congruent to 1 modulo 4?

evidence.quote: Let G_p,1 denote the induced subgraph on the vertices adjacent to the node 0, which we call the 1-localization ... It was observed empirically in [MMP19b] that ϑ(G_p,1) ∼ √(p/2) ... Conjecture 26. ϑ(G_p,1) ∼ √(p/2) (for p ≡ 1 (mod 4) prime) where G_p,1 is the 1-localization of the Paley Graph described above.

accepted.question_text: Let G_{p,2} be the induced subgraph of the Paley graph G_p on the vertices adjacent to both 0 and 1 (the 2-localization). For sufficiently large primes p ≡ 1 (mod 4), is its Lovász theta number at most (2/3)√p, i.e. does ϑ(G_{p,2}) ≤ (2/3)√p hold?

evidence.quote: Let G_p,2 denote the induced subgraph on the vertices adjacent to 0 and 1 ... Conjecture 27. For p ≡ 1 (mod 4) prime and large enough we have ϑ(G_p,2) ≤ 2/3 √p where G_p,2 is the 2-localization of the Paley Graph described above.

accepted.question_text: Does the degree-4 Sum-of-Squares relaxation for the clique number of the Paley graph beat the classical √p barrier by a polynomial factor? More precisely, does there exist ε > 0 such that the degree-4 SoS bound is O(p^{1/2−ε})?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 28. There exists ε > 0 such that the Sum-of-Squares relaxation of degree 4 for the clique number of the Paley graph gives a bound of O(p^{1/2−ε}).

accepted.question_text: Consider the Paley equiangular tight frame associated with a prime p ≡ 1 (mod 4). Does this deterministic frame satisfy a restricted isometry property beyond the square-root bottleneck: namely, is there some ε > 0 such that for m ≍ p^{1/2+ε}, every submatrix formed by choosing m distinct frame vectors has condition number bounded by a constant independent of p?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 29. The Paley Equiangular Tight Frame construction satisfies the Restricted Isometry Property beyond the square-root bottleneck. In other words, there exists ε > 0 such that, for m ∼ p^{1/2+ε}, any matrix formed by picking m (distinct) vectors in the Paley ETF has condition number bounded by a constant independent of p.

accepted.question_text: For every log-concave probability measure μ on R^n with covariance matrix A, does there exist a universal constant C > 0 such that the isoperimetric constant ψ_μ is bounded below by C / √(||A||_{op})? Equivalently, up to a universal constant, is the minimal boundary measure always attained by a half-space, as predicted by the Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits conjecture?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 30 (KLS Conjecture ([KLS95])). There exists a universal constant C > 0 such that for every log-concave measure µ, the isoperimetric constant satisfies ... Equivalently, there exists a universal constant C > 0 such that ψ_µ ≥ C / √(||A||_{op}).

accepted.question_text: Fix a finite shape α and let M_α be the associated graph matrix built from injective realizations of α into [n], with entries given by products of the corresponding edge-sign variables ε_{i,j}. Do there exist functions f(α) and g(α), depending only on α, such that the expected operator norm satisfies E||M_α|| = Θ(n^{f(α)} (log n)^{g(α)})? In particular, can one determine the correct polynomial exponent and the correct polylogarithmic factor for every fixed shape α?
accepted.context_brief: Sharp asymptotics for graph matrix norms

evidence.quote: We conjecture that given a fixed shape α, the norm of the associated graph matrix grows as a product of a polynomial and a polylogarithmic factor (depending only on α). Conjecture 31 (Sharp graph matrix bounds). There are functions f and g depending only on the shape α, such that E||M_α|| = Θ(n^{f(α)} (log n)^{g(α)}).
